nodes.summary: Over a type $\alpha$ with a boolean equality test, running an edit script on an input list processes the steps from left to right and either fails or returns an output list. A keep step with value $a$ consumes the next input value $b$ and outputs $a$; a deletion of $a$ consumes $b$ and outputs nothing; a substitution of $a$ by $c$ consumes $b$ and outputs $c$. Each of these three fails if the input is exhausted or…
nodes.title: Running an edit script

nodes.summary: The cost of an edit script is the sum of the unit costs of its steps; the empty script has cost $0$.
nodes.title: Cost of an edit script

nodes.summary: The cost of an edit step is $0$ for a keep step and $1$ for a deletion, an insertion or a substitution.
nodes.title: Unit cost of an edit step

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, write $|s|$ and $|t|$ for their lengths. The number of table-cell transitions charged by the dynamic-programming edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is exactly $(|s| + 1)(|t| + 1)$, one per pair of a prefix of $s$ and a prefix of $t$.
nodes.title: Table cost of the edit distance algorithm

nodes.title: Symmetry

nodes.summary: An edit-distance cost record is a pair of natural numbers: the number of dynamic-programming table cells initialized or transitioned, and the number of operations emitted while reconstructing an edit script.
nodes.title: Edit-distance cost counters

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the distance returned by the dynamic-programming edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is $0$ if and only if $s = t$.
nodes.title: Edit distance vanishes only on equal lists

nodes.summary: Let $s$ and $t$ be lists over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality. Every edit script that transforms $s$ into $t$ has unit cost at least the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Minimality of the computed edit distance

nodes.summary: For every list $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from the empty list to $t$ is the length of $t$.
nodes.title: Edit distance from the empty list

nodes.summary: For every list $s$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from $s$ to the empty list is the length of $s$.
nodes.title: Edit distance to the empty list

nodes.summary: Distinct lists are at positive distance.
nodes.title: Edit distance between distinct lists is positive

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, write $|s|$ and $|t|$ for their lengths. The number of reconstruction steps charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ is at most $|s| + |t|$.
nodes.title: Reconstruction cost bound for edit distance

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the number of reconstruction steps charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ equals the length of the edit script it returns.
nodes.title: Reconstruction cost of the edit distance algorithm

nodes.summary: An edit-distance result over a type $\alpha$ consists of a natural number, the reported distance, and an edit script over $\alpha$.
nodes.title: Edit-distance result record

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the edit script returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ transforms $s$ into $t$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the returned edit script

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the unit cost of the edit script returned by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$ equals the distance it returns.
nodes.title: The returned edit script realizes the distance

nodes.summary: For every list $s$ over a type whose Boolean equality test agrees with equality, the distance returned by the edit distance algorithm from $s$ to $s$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Edit distance of a list to itself

nodes.summary: For lists $s$ and $t$ over a type with a Boolean equality test, the total number of events charged by the edit distance algorithm on $s$ and $t$, that is its cell transitions plus its reconstruction steps, equals $(|s| + 1)(|t| + 1) + k$, where $k$ is the length of the edit script it returns.

nodes.title: Edit distance algorithm

nodes.summary: An edit script over a type $\alpha$ is a finite list of edit steps over $\alpha$, applied from left to right.
nodes.title: Edit script

nodes.summary: An edit step over a type $\alpha$ is one of four operations, for $a, b \in \alpha$: keep $a$ (consume the input value $a$ and reproduce it), delete $a$ (consume $a$), insert $a$ (produce $a$ without consuming input), or substitute $a$ by $b$ (consume $a$ and produce $b$).
nodes.title: Edit step

nodes.summary: Two scripts compose into one whose cost is at most the sum of their costs.
nodes.title: Composition of edit scripts is subadditive in cost

nodes.summary: Every script has an inverse of the same cost (swap insertions and deletions, reverse substitutions).
nodes.title: Every edit script has an inverse of the same cost

nodes.summary: The total of an edit-distance cost record is the number of table cells initialized or transitioned plus the number of operations emitted during reconstruction.
nodes.title: Total edit-distance cost

nodes.summary: Over a type with a boolean equality test, an edit script transforms a list $x$ into a list $y$ when running the script on $x$ succeeds and outputs $y$.
nodes.title: An edit script transforming one list into another

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
